title: Evidence preservation and incident walkthrough (scratchpad)
content:
Purpose: quick personal scratchpad for negotiating evidence-preservation, e-discovery, and forensic access clauses. Keep it short — talking points, sample language, escalation scripts.

Top-level objectives:
- Limit required on-prem/forensic actions by vendor (we host inference, they get data). prefer logs export over live access.
- Preserve chain-of-custody principles, avoid unlimited preservation windows/costs.
- Define clear notice, preservation hold, and documentation obligations.
- Carve out reasonable customer cooperation and cost allocation.

Key risks to flag:
- Broad clause that allows counterparty to demand disk images or full VM snapshots on short notice. (push back)
- Unlimited retention of full request/response payloads for arbitrary time. ask for TTL + sampling.
- For private deployments: customer-managed keys + forensic access gated by court order/escrow + SRE presence.
- Subprocessor cascade: ensure vetting + limits on 3rd-party forensic tools.

Suggested negotiation posture (one-liners to use in call):
- "We can provide structured logs and packet captures for the incident window; full disk images are high-cost and require a court order or mutual agreement."
- "Preservation hold: we will preserve relevant metadata and application logs for 90 days by default; retention extensions by written request subject to cost recovery."
- "For private/VPC: we will coordinate a time-boxed forensic snapshot with our SRE; vendor access requires a documented chain-of-custody, at-customer-site execution, or execution via a mutually-approved third party."

Sample redlines (very rough):
- "Vendor shall, upon receipt of written notice of an Incident, preserve logs, audit trails, and relevant application data for a 90-day period. Production system images or disk-level snapshots will only be produced upon: (i) mutual written agreement, or (ii) valid legal process; Vendor may recover reasonable costs for imaging and export at its standard rates."
- "Requests for raw request/response payloads will be limited to a time-bounded window and scoped by correlation ids. Vendor will provide a sampled dataset if full export is operationally disruptive."

Escalation ladder (practical):
- Triage call (1hr) — technical rep + security PM (ours) + vendor engineer (theirs)
- If forensic snapshot requested: set 48h notice + cost estimate + exec approval
- If legal process demanded: escalate to legal (ours) and request written justification + POA from counterparty

Cost recovery and rate card notes (for pitches back to legal/ops):
- Imaging/export prep (4-8 hours engineer) = chargeable hourly + storage egress
- Onsite forensic (if requested) = day rate + travel
- Emergency after-hours = 1.5x

Open questions / TODOs:
- Define exact minimal log set (auth logs, model call logs, KV cache metadata?) — sync with infra.
- Which ticket fields do we require from requestor to accept? (time range, correlation ids, business reason)
- Privacy interplay: PII in prompts — need redaction workflow if asked to produce payloads.
- What SLAs for evidence handoff? target 5 business days for structured logs; 10+ for images.

Negotiation quick scripts (tone + fallback):
- If they ask for everything: "We're committed to helping. To keep production stable and protect customer data, we provide structured exports first and can discuss discrete imaging with a signed cost agreement."
- If they push on retention: "We can agree to a limited extension for legal holds with a cost pass-through. Unlimited retention is operationally infeasible and increases risk for all parties."

Anchors/walkaways:
- Walkaway if they demand live shell access or unrestricted remote exec without court order.
- Concede limited on-prem snapshot with narrow scope and capped costs.

Notes to self (internal refs):
- Loop in infra (Rhea) for list of logs we can export cheaply.
- Draft a short annex (1 page) for IR evidence transfer and cost schedule to attach to Master Services Agreement.
- Add a checkbox flow for request intake fields in Support UI (time range, requestor contact, justification).

End of scratchpad. Keep this file short; move polished language into "legal/ir-evidence-annex" when ready.
